paragraphs: Here's what I love about this vision, friend: the powerful ones all get their turn, and then they get broken. The ram was mighty, and "No animal could stand against him" (Daniel 8:4). Then the goat came and the ram was trampled (Daniel 8:7). Then the goat's large horn snapped at the height of his power (Daniel 8:8). Kings rise, kings fall, and the whole time God is not nervous.

Even the worst of them has a limit. The insolent king gets power, but Gabriel says it "will not be his own" (Daniel 8:24). He even stands against the Prince of princes, and still Gabriel says, "Yet he will be broken off, but not by human hands" (Daniel 8:25). Evil can look like it is prospering in everything it does, and the passage tells the truth about that. It does not get the last word. The One who is over it all does.

And then there's Daniel, who ends up exhausted and sick, and still says the vision "was beyond understanding" (Daniel 8:27). I find that SO comforting, because he did not get it all and he got up anyway. He went about the king's business (Daniel 8:27). So when the Word has a part you can't figure out, baker, you don't have to. Trust that God's Word is true, stay ready, and keep doing the work in front of you, the way I keep my ovens ready.
